text:
elaine: quick question — we're tightening up SIEM export and analyst access. thinking: 1) timeboxed query leases, 2) provenance tags (request_id + owner), 3) auto-redact on export for PII, and 4) KMS-unwrap audit for any raw unwrap. has anyone implemented a flow like this? :eyes:

matt: we implemented something similar during vuln triage last year. key bits: ephemeral lease service + an export proxy that enforces redaction rules. downside: legal hold overrides need an explicit override workflow. pinging @josh for the KMS details.

josh: yup — we did per-lease CMK wrapping. flow was: requester creates lease (1h default) -> lease service provisions a wrapped ephemeral key -> analyst uses proxy to request export, proxy unwraps with audit log entry and then returns masked/exported blob. every unwrap logs request_id, lease_id, and operator. sample unwrap entry in audit: `action: kms:Decrypt, key: alias/ephemeral-lease-123, request_id: RQ-42, principal: josh, result: success`

sre-ops: important callout: the export proxy must persist provenance metadata (request_id, justification ticket, legal_hold flag) with the exported artifact. otherwise retention/forensics gets messy. also limit exports per-lease to N=2 so analysts can't exfiltrate a lot in one window.

security-bot: snapshot created for thread 1733339999 at 1733339999 by elaine. :lock:

linda: for RBAC, we used a scoped role: `analyst_temp_exporter`. policy highlights:
```
- allow: siem:view:query
- allow: siem:export:request
- allow: kms:decrypt:ephemeral-keys (condition: lease_id present)
- max_export_count: 2
- max_lease_duration: 3600
- require: justification_ticket
```
Also enforced MFA for export approval and an audit comment requirement.

josh: example API to request a lease (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://lease.internal.redwood/v1/leases \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scope":"siem-query","duration":3600,"justification":"INC-1234 vuln triage"}'
```
The response includes `lease_id` and `wrapped_key` which the proxy can pass to KMS.

matt: on redaction rules: we used a two-layer approach — rule-based scrubbing (PII regexes) + deterministic tokenization for IDs if the requestor has read access. The export policy attached `legal_hold:true` will disable tokenization and require an approval ticket and longer retention.

elaine: this is great. one more: how do you prove provenance end-to-end in case of a later audit?

josh: tie everything to the request_id stored in three places: lease service DB, proxy audit log, and export blob metadata (metadata header `X-Export-Provenance: RQ-42`). also immutably log unwrap events to our audit-log (append-only), and ship a copy to the SIEM ingestion stream with tags: `{request_id, lease_id, operator, retention_policy}`.

sre-ops: and ensure the audit-log consumer enforces retention TTLs based on the retention_policy tag. otherwise the legal team will ask why you deleted something that was supposed to be 7yrs.

linda: I'll drop a concise checklist in the docs channel later: minimal RBAC policy, sample policy snippet, curl examples, and the export request template we used for SOC approvals.

elaine: awesome — can you include the approval template that forces a JIRA link + s3 destination + expected retention? I'll start a runbook PR after that. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
